title: Holding the Dirty Thing by the Clean Side

events.speaker: narrator
events.text: Large-scale cooperation needs symbols and reasons that strangers can recognize together.

events.speaker: narrator
events.text: The book therefore treats legitimating stories as more than instruments of cynical elites.

events.speaker: narrator
events.text: Shared meanings can coordinate necessary work and make institutions possible.

events.speaker: narrator
events.text: They can also shelter privilege by presenting an unequal arrangement as inevitable.

events.speaker: narrator
events.text: The difficult task is to distinguish useful coordination from protected burden shifting.

events.speaker: narrator
events.text: Simple exposure may be insufficient when the institution solves a real collective problem.

events.speaker: narrator
events.text: The historical chapters make that ambivalence central to the inquiry.

events.speaker: narrator
events.text: Readers are asked to inspect the mechanism without assuming that every institution must fail.

events.speaker: narrator
events.text: The historical argument follows changes in the language through which authority becomes acceptable.

events.speaker: narrator
events.text: Sacred orders connect sacrifice, belonging, hierarchy, and the distribution of material benefits.

events.speaker: narrator
events.text: Modern institutions can shift the justification toward procedure, expertise, and organizational necessity.

events.speaker: narrator
events.text: The book acknowledges genuine gains in rights, public services, and predictable administration.

events.speaker: narrator
events.text: Its question is what remains concealed when the public explanation changes form.

events.speaker: narrator
events.text: A procedure may distribute responsibility so widely that no person appears accountable.

events.speaker: narrator
events.text: An efficiency argument may describe improvement while leaving the affected worker’s burden unnamed.

events.speaker: narrator
events.text: The comparison gives the reader a recurring question rather than a simple story of decline.
